feature1.prompt: acreate(), aget_or_create(), and aupdate_or_create() do not work as intended on related managers in the context of generic relations. The async-compatible interface that was added to QuerySet unintentionally exposed these async methods on the generic related managers. As a result, the methods end up invoking QuerySet functions instead of the correct manager-specific functions such as create(), get_or_create(), and update_or_create(). The required fix is to implement proper asynchronous methods that directly call the corresponding synchronous implementations provided by the generic related managers.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature focuses on modifying the asynchronous implementations for generic related managers. Developers should update the functions in django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py to ensure that acreate(), aget_or_create(), and aupdate_or_create() correctly delegate to the synchronous counterparts. The solution should follow the established pattern using sync_to_async, preserve the alters_data flag, and mirror the behavior of the synchronous methods. Reviewing the earlier async additions in the QuerySet will provide guidance on the async wrapping mechanism.
feature1.entrypoint: File to modify: django/contrib/contenttypes/fields.py. Update the function definitions for acreate(), aget_or_create(), and aupdate_or_create() so that they call the appropriate synchronous methods (create(), get_or_create(), update_or_create()) directly from the related manager. Focus on the code blocks starting around line 747 where these functions are defined, ensuring that the implementation uses sync_to_async correctly.

feature2.prompt: acreate(), aget_or_create(), and aupdate_or_create() are not operating correctly on the standard related managers because they mistakenly delegate calls to QuerySet methods. The async interface added to QuerySet inadvertently exposed these async methods on the related managers, affecting both forward and reverse relationships. This misdirection results in improper behavior for all six combinations arising from the two directions (forward and reverse). The solution is to provide proper asynchronous implementations in the related managers that invoke the correct synchronous methods directly.
feature2.hint_texts: This feature involves changes in django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py to address the asynchronous method issues in related managers. Developers should implement the async versions of create, get_or_create, and update_or_create for both forward and reverse manager scenarios. It is important to use sync_to_async appropriately and to maintain the alters_data property for these methods. The implementation must cover all six combinations stemming from the two directional relationships.
feature2.entrypoint: File to modify: django/db/models/fields/related_descriptors.py. Locate and update the definitions of acreate(), aget_or_create(), and aupdate_or_create in the sections handling related managers (around lines 793 and 1191). Ensure that the async functions for both forward and reverse relationships correctly wrap the synchronous methods using sync_to_async while preserving their data-altering behavior.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features rely on the common pattern of using sync_to_async to wrap synchronous methods and share similar alterations in Django's model layer. The changes affect the asynchronous implementations of manager methods that are used throughout the codebase.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Ensure that the async methods introduced in both generic and standard related managers follow a consistent interface. After individual development, integration tests should be run to confirm that asynchronous operations across both modules work harmoniously. Developers should agree on common patterns for error handling and the use of the alters_data flag.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers working on Feature 1 and Feature 2 should coordinate on the approach for wrapping synchronous methods asynchronously. Regular discussions are encouraged to verify that the changes in one module do not adversely affect the other and to align on testing strategies. Joint code review sessions and integration meetings are recommended to finalize the consistent behavior of async operations across related managers.
